TEN OF F_DOCS' THIRTEEN ITEMS HOLD AS WRITTEN, INCLUDING THE ONE THEY LED WITH: their refutation of 'EITHER NEGATIVE CAN LOWER A CAP' is correct and I reproduce it independently (0 lowerings over 30,025 cells, and the analytic proof max(floor,x) >= floor >= 0 makes the sweep redundant). THREE DO NOT, AND THE FIRST OF THE THREE IS THE SAME DEFECT ONE GENERATION DOWN.

HEADLINE REFUTATION -- THE PARAGRAPH WRITTEN TO END A FALSE UNIVERSAL CONTAINS THREE NEW ONES, AND THE WORST IS FALSE AT THE ONE VALUE THE PARAGRAPH ITSELF NAMES AS REACHABLE. docs/04_CONTRACT.md:566 states, unqualified, '**Below zero neither identity holds**', and gives one worked pair at cap=-100. At cap=-5 -- the cap the SAME paragraph names three lines earlier as the reachable negative one ('which `CAP_FAB_START=-5` reaches', and I confirmed new_valve resolves cap_experts=-5 with origin 'operator (fab_start=-5)') -- BOTH identities hold at the shipped levers: lift_to(-5,-0.5,8) = 3 = lift_to(-5,0,8), and lift_to(-5,0.08,-1) = -5 = lift_to(-5,0.08,0). Identity 1 holds in 21,315 of 81,920 below-zero cells I swept, 26% of the regime the sentence declares empty. The other two: 'Both negative, at a cap above zero: the max is negative and an earned lift shrinks the cap' is false in 4,444 of 81,920 cells (every one with |frac x cap| < 1 -- lift_to(1,-0.5,-100) = 1, unmoved), and 'CAP_LIFT_MIN negative alone, at a cap below zero' does not lower in 39 of 36,864 cells (lift_to(-1,0.5,-1) = -1 = lift_to(-1,0.5,0)). f_docs' finding 2 says the document now 'matches what src/capacity/api.py:411-425 and src/capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers now say in their own copies, so the three agree for the first time' -- they do agree, on a sentence that is false at the tree's own named reachable value.

TWO MORE STALE PRESENT-TENSE CLAIMS IN F_DOCS' OWN FILE, IN THE EXACT CLASS ITEM 3 WAS ABOUT, NEITHER REPORTED. (i) src/tok/levers.py:166, forty lines below the conflict (b) f_docs corrected, still reads `d_cap_lift_period Flushes, from TRAIN.batch_w x TRAIN.grow_cap_every` -- while the paragraph above it now says in as many words 'Neither the TRAIN prefix nor the Steps reading this paragraph relied on survives at either end'. There is no package TRAIN (src/train/levers.py:128 says so by name), `r["TRAIN"]` occurs zero times in assemble.py, and the row is a DIVISION not a product: derive.flush_period_windows(Windows(r['CAP'].pin_windows), r['OPT'].batch_windows). At the shipped batch_windows=1 the number is right (20000 flushes) and the arithmetic is wrong, which is this tree's stated defect definition. (ii) src/tok/levers.py:411-412 says the TOK.max_bytes -> LM.d_max_token_bytes 'Coupling is not in assemble.COUPLINGS yet, and until it is, this default agreeing with that hardcode is luck'. It IS in the table, at src/spine/assemble.py:912-931 -- and that row's own why cites 'tok/levers.py::TOKLevers records the same coupling as missing from this table', so the spine is correct and the levers file it points at is not, which is the mutual shape item 3 exists to name.

A FALSE COVERAGE CLAIM IN THE SENTENCE F_DOCS EDITED, WHICH THEIR OWN FINDING SAYS IS 'THE DEFECT THIS WHOLE ROUND IS ABOUT'. docs/04_CONTRACT.md:1803 says derive.opt_steps_from_windows 'is covered by the oracle table (575 cases, 0 mismatches, run; the two newest refusals have no oracle row yet)'. It is covered by NO oracle row at all: `ls .rework/oracle/` is eight files (_phases, blowup_stale, bwt_of, cull_gate_open, curve_verdict, forgetting_of, lift_to, pin_tick) and none is this function, and tests/test_derive.py:475 says '# NO ORACLE ROW' in as many words with its reason. The clause is inherited, but the parenthetical f_docs ADDED entrenches it by implying the older refusals are covered.

THE D17 PARAGRAPH RECORDS THE OWNER'S RULING IN THE ONE FORM UNDER WHICH THE IMPLEMENTATION COMPLIES. Every mechanical clause verified: all five accessors refuse -3 with spine.lever.LeverError naming lever and value, all five return Windows(0) at 0, FAB is stopped earlier by a build-time spine.units.UnitError out of flush_period_windows, REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD is a module constant in five api.py files. Flipping REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD is a code edit in five files; ckpt/api.py says so plainly ('an operator holding only a shell cannot reach it'). The document names the cost but restates the requirement so the cost is not a shortfall.

WHAT I CONFIRMED THAT WAS WORTH CONFIRMING. The same-commit fact is real: at a2ffc08 the five-carriers table had FOUR rows and no assemble.py row at all, and 1e8cc54 added the row AND carried the 'SIX cross-package edges' correction in assemble.py -- so no checkout ever matched the row.
